overview: The National Rural Economic Transformation Project (NRETP) is a World Bank-assisted initiative under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at promoting rural enterprises, enhancing value chains, and supporting women’s collectives in farm and non-farm sectors. It focuses on scaling up successful livelihood interventions, strengthening producer enterprises, and facilitating access to finance and markets for rural poor households. The project operates across 13 high-poverty states and supports innovation, skill development, and digital inclusion in rural economies.
objectives: Promote rural enterprises and enhance value chains in farm and non-farm sectors
Support women’s collectives and strengthen their livelihoods
Scale up successful livelihood interventions under DAY-NRLM
Strengthen producer enterprises and improve market linkages
Facilitate access to finance, credit, and financial services for rural poor
Enhance skill development and digital inclusion in rural areas
Support innovation and entrepreneurship in rural economies
Monitor and evaluate impact through robust MIS and learning systems
eligibility: The project targets rural poor households, particularly women, belonging to Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations under DAY-NRLM. Benefits are extended to producer enterprises and collectives engaged in agricultural, livestock, handicrafts, and other non-farm activities. Implementation is focused on 13 high-priority states identified based on poverty and livelihood indicators.
benefits: Beneficiaries receive support for enterprise development, access to revolving funds and credit linkages, technical assistance for value chain development, training and capacity building, market access facilitation, and infrastructure support for rural enterprises. The project also promotes digital tools for SHG management and financial inclusion through convergence with banking and financial institutions.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through revolving funds, community investment funds, and matching grants to SHGs and their federations for livelihood activities and enterprise development. Funds are channeled via State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs) and disbursed based on micro-investment plans approved at the community level. The project leverages both grant and loan components to ensure sustainability and scalability of rural enterprises.
application_process: 1. Mobilization and formation of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) at the village level under DAY-NRLM. 2. Training and capacity building of SHGs on financial literacy, livelihood planning, and enterprise development. 3. Preparation of micro-investment plans (MIPs) by SHGs for livelihood activities. 4. Appraisal and approval of MIPs by Village Organizations (VOs) and Cluster Level Federations (CLFs). 5. Disbursement of revolving funds or community investment funds to SHGs based on approved plans. 6. Monitoring and hand-holding support by SRLMs and community resource persons. 7. Linkage with banks, markets, and value chains for enterprise growth and sustainability.
required_documents: Resolution from SHG approving the MIP
Bank account details of the SHG
Identity and address proof of SHG members
Utilization certificates for previous fund disbursements (if applicable)
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on community planning cycles
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
caveats: Funds are subject to availability and approval of micro-investment plans at the community level
Benefits are restricted to households covered under DAY-NRLM in the 13 project states
Enterprise support is contingent on viability assessment and market linkage potential
Digital and innovation components may have separate eligibility and implementation timelines
